in_text_mentions: icture and pathohistological appearance. On admission excisional biopsy of lax skin has been performed. Routine hematoxylin-eosin staining has revealed normal collagen fibers, without any inflammatory infiltrate. Histopathologic analysis of skin has shown characteristic histologic feature of CL such as a loss of dermal elastic fibers revealed by orcein stain. Diminished elastic tissue was revealed throughout the dermis, not extending into the subcutis. The remaining elastic fibers were disorganized, shortened and fragmented. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A shows a posterior view of a human patient's back with visibly redundant skin folds, a classic cutaneous manifestation of cutis laxa. The article title confirms Autosomal Dominant Cutis Laxa in an adolescent male, and the caption and in-text mention specifically describe redundant skin folds over the back. The finding maps directly to cutis_laxa_generalized_skin_laxity. [raw subtype: autosomal_dominant] B: Panel B shows an anterior view of the chest and abdomen of the same human patient with prominent skin sagging, a classic cutaneous manifestation of cutis laxa. The article title confirms Autosomal Dominant Cutis Laxa in an adolescent male, and the caption and in-text mention specifically describe prominent skin sagging over the abdomen. The finding maps directly to cutis_laxa_generalized_skin_laxity. [raw subtype: autosomal_dominant]

panels.rationale: Single-panel histopathology image of a patient skin biopsy from a case report of idiopathic localized acquired cutis laxa in an adult male. Verhoeff-Van Gieson special staining shows marked to near-complete absence of elastic fibers in the dermis, indicated by arrows, which is the classic histologic hallmark of cutis laxa; the caption and in-text explicitly attribute this finding to the cutis laxa diagnosis. Real patient biopsy image, adequate quality, no third-party copyright indication. [raw subtype: localized_acquired]

panels.rationale: Single-panel chest radiograph from a case report of cutis laxa 1B presenting with giant ascending aortic aneurysm. The image shows marked enlargement of the cardiac silhouette; the in-text mentions confirm a giant ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm and massive pericardial effusion, supporting assignment of the aortic aneurysm finding in this patient. The radiographic sign itself is nonspecific, but the disease-focused article and panel-specific in-text linkage support attribution to cutis_laxa.

panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a neonate, explicitly captioned as demonstrating skin laxity and palpebral edema; in-text confirms the patient had cutis laxa (affected sibling) and that admission findings of palpebral edema, redundant skin and reduced elasticity are shown in Figure 1, in an article on cutis laxa syndrome. The image visibly shows redundant, lax skin on the face, neck, hand and trunk plus edematous eyelids, qualifying as a real untreated patient image of cutis laxa. Palpebral edema is not in the allowed vocabulary and is listed as a proposed finding; no specific cutis laxa subtype is stated in the caption or in-text, so subtype is null.

in_text_mentions: A neonate girl was born at term (3300 gram) as the second child of healthy consanguine parents. The first male baby suffered from cutis laxa and died at the age of 7 months. This female neonate was referred on the second day of life from another nursery to our hospital because of respiratory distress, skin abnormality and a palpable mass in the lower abdomen. Clinical findings at admission were palpebral edema, redundant skin and reduced elasticity (Figure 1).
